text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Friday.
LONDON - British shares bounced back to recover just over half of Thursday's losses after a rally on Wall Street. The FTSE 100 index rose 32.1 points to 4,089.5, but was down 1.5 points for the week.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index ended slightly higher, boosted by interest from German domestic fund managers and a strong performance from German bonds. At the end of the session the DAX-30 index of German blue-chip shares stood at 2,859.28 points, up 10.51 points for the day and 6.4 on the week.

PARIS - French stocks staged a partial rebound after investors were encouraged by higher bond prices and a rise on Wall Street. The blue-chip CAC-40 index, which fell 2.54 percent Thursday, rose 25.79 points or 1.14 percent to 2,282.76. For the week, it fell 24.19 points.
ZURICH - Swiss shares ended mixed with blue chips mostly lower in quiet dealings. The broad Swiss Performance Index rose 0.26 point to 2,512.14, a gain of 11.06 on the week.
TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market was closed for a holiday.

HONG KONG - Stocks edged higher, holding steady above the 13,200 level despite renewed fears on Wall Street of a hike in U.S. interest rates. The Hang Seng Index rose 19.35 points to 13,222.79 for a loss of 181.35 on the week.
SYDNEY - Australian shares fell after a volatile Wall Street kept local investors nervous. The All Ordinaries index dipped 11.7 points to 2,399.5, but was up 3.9 from last Friday.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares got hit by a drop in gold prices worldwide. The gold index fell 30.1 points to 1,458 for a loss of 37.3 for the week. The all-share index lost 19.4 points to 6,597.5, but was up 14.4 since last Friday. The industrial index added 17 points to 7,876.5, capping a gain of 61.3 for the week.
